# Editors and drive apps

An editor is a React component for the documents of one type; a drive app is the view Connect shows for a drive. Both live in `editors/<id>/`. `ph generate editor` and `ph generate app` write a stub there and register it. Your work is the UI inside the stub's files.

## Create an editor

1. Check `editors/` for an editor for the document type. If one exists, ask in an interactive session whether to create a new one or reimplement it. A model made with `ph generate document-model --name` already has a starting editor, `editors/<model>-editor/`.
2. Run `ph generate editor --name "<Name>" --document-type <type>`, e.g. `--name "Order Editor" --document-type pizza-plaza/order`. An editor has exactly one document type, and the project must hold that type's model.
3. The editor is in `editors/<editor-id>/` (the id is the kebab-cased name) and registered in `editors/editors.ts`.

## Implement the editor

The stub holds:

- `editor.tsx`: the editor. Edit this file; don't create a new main component. Keep its default-exported function named `Editor`: `ph generate editor --dir <id>` keeps a file that has one and rewrites a file that doesn't.
- `module.ts`: the module's id, name and document type. `ph generate` rewrites it on every run. Don't edit it.

Put your components in `components/` (create it), one per file. For routes, links to other documents and navigation from an editor, read the customize-connect skill's data-and-navigation guide.

Then:

- Read the model the editor is for: `document-models/<model>/v<n>/definition.ts` and its `modules/`.
- Import the model from its entry, `document-models/<model>`. Its `actions` holds the model's action creators and the base actions every document has, such as `setName`, which the stub's `editor.tsx` uses.
- Props: `EditorProps<DocumentOf<typeof Model>, ActionOf<typeof Model>>` from `document-model` gives `document` and `dispatch`, typed for the model.
- Render `<DocumentToolbar document={document} />` from `@powerhousedao/design-system/connect` first, at the top, with nothing beside it.
- Ids for new objects come from `generateId()` from `document-model`, passed in the action input.

```tsx
// editors/todo-editor/editor.tsx
import { DocumentToolbar } from "@powerhousedao/design-system/connect";
import type { ActionOf, DocumentOf, EditorProps } from "document-model";
import { Todo } from "document-models/todo";
import { TodoList } from "./components/TodoList.js";

export default function Editor({
  document,
  dispatch,
}: EditorProps<DocumentOf<typeof Todo>, ActionOf<typeof Todo>>) {
  return (
    <div>
      <DocumentToolbar document={document} />
      <TodoList document={document} dispatch={dispatch} />
    </div>
  );
}

// editors/todo-editor/components/TodoList.tsx
import type { ActionOf, DocumentOf, EditorProps } from "document-model";
import { generateId } from "document-model";
import { Todo } from "document-models/todo";

type Props = Pick<
  EditorProps<DocumentOf<typeof Todo>, ActionOf<typeof Todo>>,
  "document" | "dispatch"
>;

export function TodoList({ document, dispatch }: Props) {
  function handleAddTodo(title: string) {
    if (title) dispatch(Todo.actions.addTodo({ id: generateId(), title }));
  }
  // ...
}
```

A model that still has a `gen/` folder exports types, `actions` and hooks from its barrel instead: `TodoDocument`, `TodoAction`, `useSelectedTodoDocument()` (which returns `[document, dispatch]` in any child component), `use<Model>DocumentById`, `use<Model>DocumentsInSelectedDrive` and `use<Model>DocumentsInSelectedFolder`. There is no `editors/hooks/` folder.

`ph generate` registers every editor in `editors/editors.ts`; don't edit that file.

## Rejected actions

A reducer that throws, or a write the document's policy refuses, does not apply. To tell the user, pass `dispatch` an `onErrors` callback, as the stub's `editor.tsx` does. It gets an `OperationRejectedError` (from `@powerhousedao/reactor-browser`) per rejected action, or the error that stopped the dispatch:

- `message`: the reducer's error message, or the reason for a denial.
- `actionType`: the action's type.
- `kind`: `"reducer-error"`, or `"denied"` for a write the policy refused.

`onErrors` runs first; `onSuccess` then runs with the document and `{ rejected }`, the actions that were not applied, so clear a form only when `rejected` is empty. The types are in `@powerhousedao/shared/document-model/dispatch`. Clear the message before dispatching:

```tsx
const [error, setError] = useState<string>();

const handleRename = (title: string) => {
  setError(undefined);
  dispatch(Todo.actions.setTitle({ title }), (errors) =>
    setError(errors[0]?.message),
  );
};
```

Show the error next to the input that caused it.

## Operation history

In Connect, an editor's `document.operations` holds an empty array per scope, whatever the history. Don't read history or rejected operations from it.

- List operations with `useDocumentOperations(document.header.id, "global")` from `@powerhousedao/reactor-browser`. Pages arrive oldest first; call `fetchNextPage` while `hasNextPage` is true.
- The operation count of a scope is `document.header.revision.global` (or `[scope]`). It counts that scope's operations, rejected ones included; `revision.document` counts the document's own header operations, such as its creation.
- Connect's revision history view shows a document's operations and their errors.

## Create a drive app

A drive app is the view Connect shows for a drive: an editor module for `powerhouse/document-drive`. Read the customize-connect skill's drive-apps guide before you write the app's code: it covers the app's props and the hooks for folders, nodes and navigation.

1. Check `editors/` for an app (its `module.ts` lists `powerhouse/document-drive`). If one exists, ask in an interactive session whether to create a new one or reimplement it.
2. Run `ph generate app --name "<Name>"`. `--document-types <type>,<type>` names the types the app holds; without it the app allows every type. `--disable-drag-and-drop` turns file drops off.
3. The stub is in `editors/<app-id>/`, not `apps/`. The app id is the kebab-cased name. The module is registered in `editors/editors.ts` and `powerhouse.manifest.json`:
   - `editor.tsx`: the app's root.
   - `components/`: a folder tree, folder contents and a create button to start from.
   - `config.ts`: `allowedDocumentTypes` and `isDragAndDropEnabled`.
   - `module.ts`: the module's id, name and document type.

## Implement the drive app

- The stub is written once. While `editor.tsx` has its default-exported `Editor` function, `ph generate app --dir <app-id>` leaves `editor.tsx`, `components/`, `config.ts` and `module.ts` alone and only re-registers the module. Edit them freely.
- To change the types the app holds, edit `allowedDocumentTypes` in `config.ts`.
- Read the customize-connect skill's drive-apps guide before writing code. It covers the app's props (`document` is the drive, `children` is the open document's editor or `null`), the `@powerhousedao/reactor-browser` hooks for folders, nodes and navigation, and how a drive gets its app.

## Attach an app to a drive

A drive shows the app its `header.meta.preferredEditor` names.

- New drive: `addDrive` with `{ "name": "<name>", "preferredEditor": "<app-id>" }`.
- Existing drive: `addActions` on the drive with `{ "type": "SET_PREFERRED_EDITOR", "scope": "header", "input": { "preferredEditor": "<app-id>" } }`.

The Create Drive dialog, drives every user gets (`connect.drives.defaultDrives`), setting the app from code and Connect's default view are in the customize-connect skill's drive-apps guide.

## Check your work

Run `npm run tsc` and `npm run lint:fix` after creating or changing an editor or app.
